thread:
acme-integrations: Hey @jess — started seeing our ingest pipeline fail after last night's rollout. Fields that used to be arrays (order_items, metadata.events) are now being returned as JSON-encoded strings (escaped). Happening for ~30% of requests. Sample request id: req_0a9f1b2c. No changes on our side, this is blocking downstream ETL.

jess-cs: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you paste the exact API call you made, the model/version header, and a small example of the response body you are seeing? Also any request ids and timestamps help.

acme-integrations: Sure — reproducer below. We call the generate endpoint with a prompt that requests strict JSON. Note X-Model-Version header in our call.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Model-Version: text-2.3" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Return a JSON object with keys: order_id (string), order_items (array of objects), total (number).","max_tokens":200}'
```

Response we get (excerpt):
```json
{
  "output": {
    "order_id": "ord-123",
    "order_items": "[{\"id\":1,\"qty\":2},{\"id\":5,\"qty\":1}]",
    "total": 42.5
  }
}
```

This used to be delivered as an array:
```json
"order_items": [{"id":1,"qty":2},{"id":5,"qty":1}]
```

Now our JSON parser throws: Unexpected token "[" in JSON at position ... because order_items is a string.

matt-eng-ml: tagging in here. Thanks for the repro, @acme-integrations and @jess. Timing question — when you say "last night's rollout", do you have an approximate timestamp? We had a runtime config push (structured-output sanitizer defaults) at 1971119000 UTC.

acme-integrations: The failures start around 1971120000 UTC for our logs. Request id above is from 1971120175.

matt-eng-ml: I pulled the request id and replayed it against text-2.3 locally with the same headers. I can reproduce the stringified nested JSON. Quick hypothesis: a change in the structured-output postprocessor switched from strict schema injection to a relaxed serialization for certain content, and nested arrays are being serialized to strings when the model emits ambiguous delimiters.

matt-eng-ml: Short-term workaround: add schema_enforcement: "strict" to the request body or pin the model header to text-2.2 while we patch. Example: { "prompt":..., "schema_enforcement": "strict" } — that forces the postprocessor to coerce types and unwrap encoded JSON. Can you try?

jess-cs: Passed workaround to customer and opened internal ticket CS-9182. Noted that this correlates with config push at 1971119000.

acme-integrations: Confirmed — adding schema_enforcement: "strict" in the request fixes the immediate problem. Downstream parser is back to normal. Thank you. Please advise when there is a proper fix; we can't rely on pinning older models long-term. :heart:

matt-eng-ml: We're starting a rollback/patch. Plan: 1) revert sanitizer default to strict for rollout group, 2) push a unit/regression test for nested arrays, 3) ship patch and validate. ETA 3-4 hours. I'll update this thread when patch is deployed.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: rollout runtime-config@v2.3.4 by ryan — started at 1971123380 — note: this is a partial rollforward of the config change mentioned above.

matt-eng-ml: After the rollback we validated against the customer's request and confirmed arrays are now returned as arrays. We'll keep schema_enforcement strict by default while we work on a safer relaxed mode.

jess-cs: Customer notified. Closing interim CS ticket; keeping engineering bug open (ENG-12451) until we add tests and a feature flag.

acme-integrations: Thanks everyone — workaround and rollback both worked. Please share postmortem when available.
